content:
The Women's team archery event at the 2012 Summer Olympics took place at Lord's Cricket Ground in London from July 27-29, 2012.

**Key Details:**

**Gold Medal:** South Korea (Ki Bo-bae, Lee Sung-jin, Choi Hyeonju)
- This was South Korea's 7th consecutive Olympic gold medal in women's team archery (every Olympics since 1988)
- They defeated China 210-209 in a very close final

**Silver Medal:** China (Cheng Ming, Fang Yuting, Xu Jing)

**Bronze Medal:** Japan (Miki Kanie, Ren Hayakawa, Kaori Kawanaka)
- Japan defeated Russia 209-207 in the bronze medal match

**Competition Format:**
- 12 teams qualified based on the results from the individual ranking round
- Teams consisted of three archers each
- The competition used a single-elimination bracket
- Each match consisted of shooting 24 arrows per team (8 per archer)
- Teams shot in groups of 6 arrows (2 per archer) alternating between teams

**Notable Moments:**
- The gold medal match was exceptionally close, with South Korea winning by just one point
- This continued South Korea's complete dominance in Olympic women's team archery
- The event took place at the historic Lord's Cricket Ground, which was temporarily converted into an archery venue

The South Korean team's victory maintained their perfect Olympic record in this event, having never lost the women's team competition since it was introduced to the Olympic program.
